title: Incremental KV shadow checkpoints for GPU-resident prompt cache
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem:
Redwood's serving runtime builds and reuses KV state from prior prompt context to amortize cost when multiple requests share leading context. Current approaches either keep full copies in CPU memory and page shards to GPUs (high transfer overhead), or aggressively evict to reduce residency (high cold-start token cost). Both strategies cause either elevated per-token latency for overlaps or excessive GPU memory pressure under concurrent sessions.

Goal:
Create a lightweight, incremental checkpointing mechanism (KV shadow checkpoints) that allows overlapping prompt context to be reconstructed in-GPU with minimal transfers and deduplication, enabling continuous batching to benefit from high overlap while keeping GPU resident working set small and predictable. Key goals: reduce inter-request duplication of KV blobs, enable partial updates without full copy-on-write, and provide safe rollbacks for canary/rollback semantics.

Design overview (high level):
1) Content-hash journaling: KV fragments are written once and referenced by content hash. A lightweight journal records fragment references for each session or request. Journals are small and stored in CPU with compact deltas.
2) Shadow checkpoint layers: instead of copying whole KV for each request, create thin checkpoint layers that record only newly materialized fragments (append-only). When reconstructing in GPU, merge layers by following references; identical fragments are reused by pointer.
3) Chunked GPU residency: fragments are sharded into fixed-size chunks (e.g., 64–256KB). Residency is managed at chunk granularity to reduce internal fragmentation and allow partial eviction/refresh during long-running requests.
4) Incremental snapshot transfer: when a request requires KV state not present on-device, only missing chunk references are fetched and assembled; prefetch heuristics request likely-future chunks during the attention loop for long sequences.
5) Continuous-batching compatibility: the journal and layer model are compatible with continuous-batching: the batch coordinator can produce a merged view for the GPU runtime by resolving pointers without duplicating data per batch slot.

Implementation details (initial plan):
- On write path: when a KV fragment is materialized, compute a stable 64-bit content hash (fast non-cryptographic checksum + length) and register in a global fragment ledger. If fragment exists, increment refcount and return reference id. Otherwise, persist fragment to CPU cache store (content-addressed) and create thin layer entry.
- On request assembly: resolve session's active journal layers to a set of chunk references. Query per-GPU residency map; issue point-requests for chunks missing on-device using RDMA/GPU direct path where available. Assemble pointers into GPU-resident index (no copy if identical pointer exists).
- Eviction policy: LRU by chunk with awareness of active layer references and predicted reuse score from continuous-batching telemetry. Avoid evicting chunks referenced by in-flight layers.
- Rollback & canary: keep recent checkpoints (configurable window in layers) so canary rollouts can reconstitute prior views without forcing full recompute.

Telemetry and correctness checks:
- Track per-chunk refcounts, per-layer size, assembly latency, and bytes transferred per-request.
- Add unit tests for pointer-equality reuse, checkpoint layering semantics, and race conditions during concurrent writes and evictions.
- Staging workload: replay production request traces (sampled) in a sandbox env to validate assembly latencies and memory pressure.

Trade-offs considered:
- Content-hash collision risk: using a non-cryptographic checksum is fast but has tiny collision probability; mitigate by including length and a 16-bit secondary fingerprint for sanity checks.
- Extra indirection cost: pointer-based assembly adds a small pointer chase on request startup vs flat copy; we expect this to be outweighed by avoided memory transfers for high-overlap workloads.
- Metadata overhead: journals/layers add CPU RAM overhead. We cap entries and compact stale layers periodically.

Rollout plan and milestones:
- Spike (1 week): prototype chunked content-hash store and reference ledger; microbench KV write and read paths. (Spike branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/xxxx)
- Alpha (2 sprints): integrate into runtime in a sandbox mode behind a feature flag, add telemetry, and run replay tests.
- Beta (1 sprint): expose safe default eviction thresholds, enable incremental prefetch during continuous batches, and run customer workload pilots.
- Gradual rollout: start with low-traffic host-tier and monitor bytes transferred, average per-request KV assembly latency, and GPU residency.

Acceptance criteria:
- Net decrease in average bytes transferred per request for sampled production traces with >20% overlap.
- Median KV assembly added latency < 3ms for common cases (when most chunks are resident).
- No increase in regressions (error rates) related to memory corruption; zero data loss in canary rollback tests.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Chunk size sweet spot for balancing pointer table size vs transfer overhead (64KB vs 256KB) — need perf matrix.
- Durability: should the CPU content-addressed store be backed by SSD for very large working sets, or rely on recomputation?
- Strong vs eventual refcount consistency across multi-GPU hosts — pick relaxed refcount with periodic reconciliation to avoid stalls.

Links to artifacts:
- Design doc (Draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Incremental+KV+Shadow+Checkpoints
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4127 (WIP)
comments: 2026-02-26 - Spike started: built quick content-hash ledger and simple chunking. Observed ~28% bandwidth reduction in synthetic overlap trace for 128KB chunks.

2026-03-02 - Design review with Runtime team: Alex R. suggested adding a 16-bit secondary fingerprint to reduce collision risk; PM requests telemetry for customer-visible metrics. Action: add secondary fingerprint and telemetry hooks.
2026-03-04 - Infra sync: Arjun confirmed RDMA path available on dedicated infra; will gate RDMA use behind runtime capability check. Action item: detect and prefer GPU direct when possible.

2026-03-08 - Security review request queued: identified that journals contain no PII but may include hashed prompt fragments. Security stated 'low' risk and requested encryption-at-rest for CPU cache. Adding to TODOs.
2026-03-10 - Implementation update: initial assembler built; unit tests for pointer reuse passing locally. Performance harness being prepared to run against sampled traces this week.
